raw_segments.text: The same causes which, in the progress of improvement, gradually raise the price of
butcher's meat, should have the same effect, it may be thought, upon the prices of wool
and raw hides, and raise them, too, nearly in the same proportion.
It probably would be so if, in the rude beginnings of improvement, the market for the latter
commodities was confined within as narrow bounds as that for the former.
But the extent of their respective markets is commonly extremely different.
